choices: Saves uncommitted tracked changes and cleans the working tree
items.explain: Stash push stores dirty tracked work on the stash stack and resets the working tree toward HEAD.

items.prompt: git stash pop compared with git stash apply…
choices: Pop applies the stash and removes it from the list; apply keeps the entry
Pop only works on remotes; apply only works locally
They are identical in every case
items.explain: Pop = apply + drop the top stash entry; apply leaves the stash on the stack.

items.prompt: By default, git stash includes untracked files.
items.explain: Default stash covers tracked dirty files; use stash push -u to include untracked files.

items.prompt: A common reason to stash is…
choices: You need a clean tree to switch branches or pull mid-edit
You never plan to restore the changes
You are editing the syllabus only
items.explain: Stash pauses local work so you can change context, then pop or apply to resume.
